questions.q: What does the Apply to each action require before it can run?
options: A Do until action nested above it
An array — a list of items, such as emails or SharePoint records, returned by an earlier action
A scheduled trigger specifically
At least two conditions already configured
questions.explain: Apply to each runs its inner actions once for every item in an array. That array must already exist, produced by an earlier action like Get emails (V3).

questions.q: Castlebridge wants to poll a shipment-tracking API every few minutes until the status finally comes back "Delivered." There's no list of items involved, just a single status to wait on. Which loop fits?
options: Apply to each
Do until
Neither — this requires a condition with no loop
A scheduled trigger alone, with no loop needed
questions.explain: Do until repeats actions until a specified condition becomes true, which fits waiting on a single changing state rather than looping over a fixed list.

questions.q: Why do Do until's Count and Timeout settings matter?
options: They determine which array the loop runs over
They convert Do until into an Apply to each loop
They are safety limits that stop a loop from running indefinitely if its condition never becomes true
They are required fields with no functional effect
questions.explain: Count and Timeout cap how many iterations or how much time a Do until loop can consume, preventing an endless loop if the condition is never satisfied.

questions.q: If a Get emails (V3) action is configured with Top set to 10, how many times will an Apply to each loop built on its output run?
options: Exactly once, regardless of Top
Zero times, since Top only affects sorting
Once for every item in the array it receives — up to 10 times, matching the Top value
Ten times no matter how many emails actually exist
questions.explain: Apply to each runs once per item in its array. With Top set to 10, the array can contain up to 10 emails, so the loop runs once for each one actually returned.

questions.q: Because Do until checks its condition at the end of each iteration rather than the beginning, what does that guarantee?
options: The loop never runs its actions
The actions inside the loop always run at least once
The condition is evaluated before any action runs, every time
The loop automatically becomes an Apply to each
questions.explain: Because Do until evaluates its condition after each pass rather than before, the actions inside always execute at least one time, even if the condition was already true to begin with.
